articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: A CISA contractor literally left the keys to the digital kingdom sitting on GitHub like a drunk intern's personal diary. When the agency responsible for cybersecurity can't secure their own AWS creds, you know we're living in peak irony.

articles.title: Fake Android Apps Commit Carrier Billing Fraud for Premium Svcs.
articles.summary: GitHub got pwned by TeamPCP who made off with 4,000 internal repos like digital pirates raiding the mothership. The platform that hosts everyone's secrets couldn't keep their own locked down.

articles.title: GitHub Internal Repositories Breached via Malicious Nx Console VS Code Extension
articles.summary: A 9-year-old Linux kernel vuln finally crawled out of the digital basement to enable root command execution. Sometimes the best backdoors are the ones hiding in plain sight for nearly a decade.

articles.title: Microsoft Open-Sources RAMPART and Clarity to Secure AI Agents During Development
articles.summary: Drupal's 'highly critical' PostgreSQL flaw opens the RCE floodgates with a CVSS 6.5 score. Because apparently content management systems and databases together create beautiful security disasters.

articles.title: Microsoft Releases Mitigation for YellowKey BitLocker Bypass CVE-2026-45585 Exploit
articles.summary: Microsoft's BitLocker got bypassed by the 'YellowKey' flaw, proving once again that when Redmond says 'encrypted,' they mean 'temporarily inconvenienced.' Full-disk encryption becomes full-disk suggestion.

articles.title: Microsoft Took a Step Toward Human Rights Accountability. Google and Amazon (and Others) Should Pay Attention!
articles.summary: EFF celebrates an encrypted messaging victory in their newsletter, because apparently we still have to fight for the radical concept of private conversations. End-to-end encryption: not just for paranoids anymore.

articles.title: Your Privacy Shouldn't Be A Corporate Decision
articles.summary: Microsoft actually took a baby step toward human rights accountability while Google and Amazon continue their surveillance capitalism world tour. When Microsoft looks ethical by comparison, you know the bar is underground.

articles.title: Cyber Pros Can't Decide If AI Is a Good or a Bad Thing
articles.summary: EFF drops a new guide on fighting digital surveillance abuses because apparently we need instruction manuals to remember that mass surveillance is bad. When basic human rights require how-to guides, democracy is debugging itself.

articles.title: Ahmadinejad Is Still Bad for Iranians — and Still Great for Israel
articles.summary: Critical OT robot vulnerability lets attackers play puppet master with industrial systems through command injection. Because nothing says 'secure critical infrastructure' like unauthenticated remote robot hijacking.

articles.title: Open Records Laws Reveal ALPRs’ Sprawling Surveillance. Now States Want to Block What the Public Sees.
articles.summary: Casepoint launches AI-powered FOIA tools, which is either the future of government transparency or another way to automate the runaround. At least the robots will redact documents more efficiently than humans.
